sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.12% (+11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.79% (+3 bp); 2s10s curve +33 bp (+8 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.06% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.70 (+1.3% in a month, +3.5% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.036 (-1.5% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.664 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.61 (+8.1%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.1% in a month (+13.3% YTD); VIX 16.7. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy

econ.title: Unemployment Claims
econ.why: Labor market sets the Fed path, dollar and demand

us_econ: Inflation: CPI 3.7% y/y (2026-09), core 2.6%; core 3-month annualized 3.4%; core PCE 3.0%. Jobs: payrolls +29k in 2026-09 (3-month average +51k), unemployment 4.2% (+0.1), wages 3.0% y/y. Growth: real GDP 2.2% annualized in 2026-Q2, consumer spending 3.8%. Policy: fed funds target 3.75-4.0% (effective 3.88%); 2-year Treasury 4.79% (+0.91 vs fed funds: market pricing hikes); 10-year breakeven inflation 2.35%, real 10-year 2.77%. Farm prices (PPI farm products) +1.5% y/y; food-at-home CPI +1.8% y/y. For ags: high real yields and a firm dollar weigh on fund demand for commodities; sticky inflation keeps rates high (carry and storage costs up); a weak job market or falling real incomes hits meat and dairy demand first.

energy.read: 3-2-1 crack $54.33/bbl (ULSD $102.19, gasoline $30.39). For ags: diesel and natural gas set farm fuel, drying and nitrogen fertilizer costs; crude and gasoline drive ethanol and biodiesel margins (corn, soybean oil).
